title: hire enumerate should ask the daemon, not build its own registry
description:
hire/src/main.rs:159-184 builds an attestor registry in-process and calls enumerate() directly, so 'hire enumerate' reports what THIS PROCESS can see, not what the running daemon sees. The two can differ: the daemon may have started under a different environment, a different session, or before a device was plugged in. A user debugging 'why does hired not see my key' is shown the wrong answer by the tool they would naturally reach for.

Once the candidate-listing RPC exists (persona-jl4j.4), enumerate becomes a client of it and the divergence closes.

Keep a way to run the local probe explicitly -- it is genuinely useful for 'is this box capable' as distinct from 'is the daemon seeing it' -- but it must not be the default, and the output must say which question it answered.
acceptance_criteria: hire enumerate reports the daemon's view by default; the in-process probe is still reachable under an explicit flag; the output names which of the two it is showing.
